raw.body:
After exploring some of the compiler source I realized this is probably intended behavior. It all got a bit technical, but I think the shortest explanation that is easy to understand is:

Given the component props:

```ts
{
  nodes: [],
  selection: { node: null },
}
```
The callback `n => n.id === selection?.node.id` would never run, ensuring the invalid access of `node.id` would not throw an error.

React compiler code may not alter this behavior; if it were to try and access `id` even when `nodes.length === 0`, the compiled component would now throw.

Adding the unconditional evaluation of `selection?.node.id` makes the component throw regardless of the compiler check. That sounds bad, but it means the compiler is now free to depend on that same read; if it fails it wouldn't make a difference.

In my example, I typed `selection.node` to be non-nullable. I failed to realize the compiler does not and should not rely on static types.

---

I'm not sure if I should close this issue, or if it maybe should be a feature request? Seeing that the compiler code knows exactly what's going on, it feels like we can also make it understand when the callback passed to `find` runs?
